synopsis: Unreal Engine 5 is available in simulation tooling: CARLA switched from UE4 to UE5, though some APIs are unsupported, and VTD 2025.1 added UE5 rendering [f8892, f8428]. The CARLA release information found includes the 0.10.0 UE5 line dated 19 December 2024 and version 0.9.16 dated 16 September 2025 [f9013]. CARLA on UE5 requires an NVIDIA RTX 3000-series GPU or better, at least 16 GB VRAM and 130 GB disk; the glossary contrasts that VRAM minimum with 48 GB cloud GPUs and 96 GB workstation cards [f8850, f16177, f16195]. ISPRS 2024 reported UE5 3DGS performance of 60 FPS for a single building versus 17 FPS for a 23-million-Gaussian terrain scene, providing scene-dependent performance results relevant to hardware-in-the-loop testing [f3893, f3894, f3764]. Open-source platforms offering UE5 rendering and RTX sensors are reported as free for internal use, but the agriculture examples—including UE5 plant simulation presented at a CVPR 2024 workshop—do not establish applicability to heavy construction-machine braking [f9336, f9337, f4146, f4148].
